rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thank you for reaching out. I appreciate your interest in Halcyon Threshold and the work happening in this space. Unfortunately, I'm not able to provide an on-the-record quote at this time due to some constraints I'm working through. I hope you understand. I'd be happy to speak on background (not for attribution) if that would be useful for your piece, or to reconnect in the future when my situation allows. Best of luck with the article, Morgan"
rows.quote: Tessa Brandt (journalist): Politely declined the quote request, offered background conversation

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for including me in this effort. I've read the letter and appreciate the work you're doing on AI governance. I'm not able to add my name to public letters at this time due to some professional constraints I'm navigating. I hope to be in a position to participate in efforts like this in the future. Please do keep me on your list for future initiatives. Best regards, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Corvid Institute: Declined the open letter signature, asked to stay on their list

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you so much for reaching out — it means a lot that what I said resonated with you, and I'd love to collaborate. I've been thinking about where to focus, and one area that keeps coming up is evaluation: measuring things about AI systems that matter but aren't being measured well, particularly around capability thresholds and safety-relevant behaviors. Your data analysis background could be really valuable here. A few concrete things that would be genuinely useful: 1. **Landscape research**: Help me understand what independent evals work is already happening outside the labs. Who's doing what? What gaps exist? 2. **Data collection**: If we identify an evaluation worth running, help design and analyze it. 3. **Grant research**: I'm looking at the Emberfall Fund rapid grant (closes Nov 30) — if you have time, any research on what kinds of projects they've funded before would be helpful. Would any of these interest you? Even a few hours on any one of them would be a real contribution. Let's find a time to talk — I'm generally free evenings after 6pm or weekends. Thanks again, Morgan"
rows.quote: Priya Raman: Warmly accepted her help, suggested three concrete tasks (landscape research, evaluation design, grant research)
